articles.title: Gen Z shatters America's political orthodoxies
This is Trump's pride and joy — and destroying it must be the next president's first job
articles.description: The White House is supposed to be a beacon of power and strength on the global stage, a paragon of democracy standing against all enemies, both foreign and domestic. Until Trump moved in and decided to demolish that image, because he’s an ingrate who hates America. Trump’s renovations of the People’s House never should’ve happened in the first place, because that’s OUR house, not his. He’s not the owner; we are. He’s a temporary squatter who doesn’t deserve to breathe the air within those glorified halls. The president is supposed to get Congressional approval before making any major renovations to the White House have to be approved by Congress, but since Trump never listens to anyone, he went ahead and did it anyway. I burst into tears when I first saw images of what he's done with that ballroom construction, a perfect visual metaphor for Trump’s “bull in a china shop” approach to destroying our government and all of our American norms. How did this happen? I screamed into the social media abyss over and over about how demoralizing that image is, which was his intention all along. How does he get away with something this egregiously treasonous? Republicans said nothing. NOTHING. Their silence as compliance emboldened him to do the most destruction to the White House since British troops set it on fire during the War of 1812. They’ve also been vocal supporters of Trump’s Epstein Ballroom Bunker, which no other president ever needed, leading to questions as to why the ground was ever broken for it. Those questions are even more important to ask this week, as a new aerial photo of the grounds caused shockwaves on social media. That ballroom is now bigger than the White House itself, and I don’t understand how anyone is fine with his deliberate vandalization of Washington. Republicans are infuriatingly silent about this, just like they were when Trump began to tackify the Oval Office with gold-plated crap all over the place as if he looted a clearance sale at a Hobby Lobby in Moscow. They said nothing when Trump demolished the East Wing of the White House, and we have no idea if the historical artifacts collected by all the First Ladies have been properly preserved. According to the White House Historical Association, a detailed photographic record and a comprehensive 3D/digital scanning project of the East Wing and its surrounding gardens was completed before the wrecking ball was deployed. All of the artifacts were allegedly “carefully removed, cataloged, and placed into curatorial storage” by the White House curator, her staff, and the chief usher. However, reports from POLITICO have highlighted “ongoing public debate, scrutiny, and speculation regarding the transparency and public accessibility of the stored artifacts.” So the answer is we probably won’t be able to find out where they are until we have a Democratic president again, unless the next Democratic Congress wants to open an investigation. The House Natural Resources Committee has oversight authority over the Interior Department and federal lands and grounds, and would be the best choice for investigating both the White House ballroom and East Wing demolition. The current ranking Democrat, Rep. Jared Huffman of California, is poised to take over as Chair, and I’d love to see him open an investigation into everything Trump has done on the White House grounds. Over in the Senate, the Energy and Natural Resources Committee could also look into that. My Senator, Ron “Chutzpah” Wyden (D-OR), currently sits on that Committee and will also be the ranking Democrat on the Senate Finance Committee in January, so I think that’s something I should bring up with him the next time I get the chance to chat with him. But Trump wasn’t done with just demolishing the White House itself, so he also paved over the Rose Garden to make it look like another tacky patio at Mar-A-Lago, just without a pool. And then he turned the South Lawn into a traveling parking lot carnival trailer park. And nothing but cheers from the same racist losers who screamed when Barack Obama built a basketball court, and Michelle Obama planted a vegetable garden. How was he ever allowed to bring in a construction crew in the first place? There should be a deeper dive into the embarrassment of America’s 250th Birthday celebration, where a UFC cage still sat on the White House lawn after Trump invited sweaty, shirtless men to beat each other up on his birthday. All of this vandalism was a gift to his Daddy Vladdy to make America look as weak as possible on the global stage. And then there’s Algaegate, aka the Problems With the Reflecting Pool, caused by Trump himself, because he can’t leave things alone and only makes things worse when he tries to “fix” them. I mean, he hired a pool guy who looked like a Dick Tracy villain, so you can’t tell me he wasn’t trying to make it worse on purpose. When Democrats start declaring their candidacies in 2028, tearing down that eyesore bunker and restoring the White House to its original glories should be one of their top priorities. In a world that’s now dominated by visuals, the image of the White House matters more than ever. It should never look like the “before” photo on an HGTV show about restoring old homes. Any “improvements” should actually look like they’ve improved our image in the media and on the world stage. You know, like GROWING VEGETABLES AND ROSES IN GARDENS. Nobody should accept Trump’s deliberate destruction of our White House, and that includes anyone still supporting him. If he truly loved America, he’d have left it standing the way it is out of respect for the office, or would have only added things to beautify the already hallowed grounds. Instead, he’s treating the White House like he’s putting in an ADU behind Mar-a-Lago without paying for any of the permits and stiffing all of the contractors. There must be accountability.

articles.title: Duffy national address falls apart just as it started: 'This is our kind of, um, day'
articles.description: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy’s press conference on Saturday started disastrously. The Donald Trump appointee had only just started thanking air traffic controllers for their work during the crisis when feedback began blaring through the microphone at Transportation Department headquarters, the Washington Post reported. Duffy paused, tried again, and was forced to stop a second time. “Oh, this is not operational?” he asked. “This is our kind of, um, day.” Most news outlets cut away while staff scrambled to fix the sound, according to Mediaite. Minutes later the livestream returned, with Duffy counting from one to seven into the microphone before he pressed on, the report notes. The glitch came as airlines scrapped thousands more flights Saturday, a day after the FAA froze all departures for more than four hours. It was only the second nationwide ground stop since 9/11. Once the briefing got going, Duffy blamed contractor L3Harris. He said a router installed during a copper-to-fiber upgrade at a remote FAA site had flooded the network. He added that officials still didn’t know whether installation error or faulty equipment was at fault. L3Harris did not immediately respond to NPR’s request for comment. The appearance was Duffy’s second try at explaining the meltdown. A Friday night White House briefing alongside Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin had drawn widespread criticism, including griping from White House insiders.

Mary Peltola nears an Alaska Senate win as Democrats eye a 56th seat
articles.description: Democrat Mary Peltola has widened her lead over Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan in Alaska's still-undecided U.S. Senate race, moving within striking distance of an outright victory that would give Democrats their 56th Senate seat following sweeping midterm gains. As of Saturday morning, Peltola had 49.8% of the vote, compared with Sullivan's 46.1%, a margin of more than 10,000 votes. The Associated Press reported 96% of votes counted, with Peltola receiving 138,240 votes to Sullivan's 127,828. The former congresswoman gained nearly 2,000 votes on Sullivan in the latest batch of ballots, strengthening her prospects of clearing the 50% threshold needed to avoid Alaska's ranked-choice voting tabulation. Peltola's campaign declared victory Friday, insisting the Republican incumbent could no longer overcome her advantage. "There is no mathematical path for Sullivan to win this race," the campaign said in a statement posted on X. "When the remaining votes are counted, Mary will decisively be elected as Alaska’s next United States Senator," the statement read. Campaign manager Cheryl Bruce echoed that confidence in a statement to Newsweek. "As more ballots get counted, it’s clear that Mary’s victory is all but guaranteed, and Alaskans have resoundingly rejected Dan Sullivan’s D.C. self dealing," Bruce said. "Mary won today’s ballot drop by a decisive margin, and remaining votes from Anchorage, Juneau, and rural Alaska will continue to break for Mary, continuing her momentum to the United States Senate. "Alaskans are ready for a senator who fights to lower costs and takes on D.C. corruption, and when every vote is counted, Mary will deliver for Alaska," Bruce said. Sullivan's campaign, however, declined to concede. "We’re still waiting for every ballot to be counted. And we’ll see what happens from there," campaign spokesman Nate Adams told The New York Times on Friday. The race remained uncalled Saturday, with outstanding ballots potentially determining whether Peltola secures an outright majority or must prevail through ranked-choice voting. Under Alaska's system, if no candidate receives more than 50% of first-choice votes, the lowest-performing candidates are eliminated and their supporters' subsequent preferences redistributed until a winner emerges. Two minor candidates, Republican Gerald Heikes and unaffiliated Daniel J. Sullivan Jr., have collectively captured roughly 4% of the vote. Democrats recruited both candidates in an effort to weaken the incumbent's support, according to The New York Times. The Trump administration previously challenged the election over the presence of another candidate named Sullivan, arguing potential voter confusion, but the lawsuit was dismissed. Alaska has until Nov. 18 to complete its vote count, with ranked-choice tabulation to follow if necessary. A Peltola victory would represent another significant Democratic pickup in a midterm election that has already delivered the party 55 Senate seats, its largest majority since the early Obama administration. Peltola, who campaigned on "fish, family, and freedom," would become the first Alaska Native elected to the Senate and the first Democrat to win an Alaska Senate seat in nearly two decades. Her potential victory would also underscore Republican difficulties in a state President Donald Trump carried by approximately 14 percentage points in 2024, amid voter concerns over high prices, the administration's war in Iran, and tariffs affecting Alaska's economy. In another major Democratic victory in Alaska, former state lawmaker Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins, 37, has won the state's gubernatorial election, defeating three Republican opponents in a four-way contest, according to Decision Desk HQ. Kreiss-Tomkins will succeed term-limited Republican Gov. Mike Dunleavy, becoming Alaska's youngest governor and the first Democrat elected to the office in more than two decades. His victory came after national political organizations poured millions into the contest, with Democrats benefiting from a divided Republican field despite Trump's endorsement of Bernadette Wilson. Meanwhile, Alaska's U.S. House race remains uncalled, with Republican Rep. Nick Begich III leading in a contest expected to proceed to ranked-choice tabulation. © 2026 Newsmax. All rights reserved.
